title: So You Want To Talk About Race

questions.q: According to Ijeoma Oluo, when should you treat an issue as being about race?
a: When a person of color says it is, no questions asked
Only when someone uses an explicitly racist slur
Only when a court or official body rules that it is
When people of different races disagree about it
questions.why: Lesson 1 says that if a person of color thinks an issue is about race, it is, without further debate.

questions.q: What does Oluo recommend doing at the start of a conversation about race?
a: Explain why you want to talk so the other person can decide to engage
Ask the other person to explain their experiences first
Keep your reasons private so the talk feels natural
Wait until the other person raises the subject themselves
questions.why: Lesson 2 advises stating your reasons up front so the other person can choose whether to take part.

questions.q: What else does the summary say you should do before a conversation about race?
a: Research the topic yourself rather than expecting others to educate you
Rehearse your arguments so you can win the discussion
Bring a friend along to support your point of view
Wait until you feel completely free of bias
questions.why: Lesson 2 says it is not the job of people of color to explain things you could look up yourself.

questions.q: What does the summary identify as the first step of the school-to-prison pipeline?
a: Suspension, which breaks kids’ trust in school
Poor grades in core academic subjects
A lack of after-school activities
Placement in special education classes
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the pipeline begins with suspension, which damages trust and self-esteem.

questions.q: How does racial bias show up in school discipline, according to the summary?
a: Children of color are punished more often and more harshly than white children
White children are suspended for minor misbehavior more often
All students receive the same punishment for the same offense
Teachers avoid punishing anyone for minor misbehavior
questions.why: Lesson 3 reports that administrators punish children of color more often and more severely for even small things.
